ground_truth_core_content:
Introduction:
**1:** Both sections cover the same core ideas: anchoring in the two capstones (Nova, Brown), the risks of a late or wrong framework choice (brittle abstractions, stalled progress, hidden durability gaps), the two recurring concepts (LangGraph interrupts/checkpoints vs. MCP interoperability), and the architecture preview (research agent as lightweight MCP server, writing agent as durable workflow exposing coarse-grained MCP tools). The generated section frames the lesson's focus as "philosophies, core abstractions, and production trade-offs" without explicitly negating API-syntax/hello-world framing the way the guideline phrases it, but the substance of the focus statement is the same.

Framework Choice Under Uncertainty and Why Some Selection Strategies Fail in Production:
**1:** Both sections cover the same three-layer distinction (runtime/protocol/tooling) and the production problem each solves, the two hype-driven failure modes (too simple vs. too complex), and end with the same capstone pivot story used near-verbatim. The generated section adds an extra illustrative paragraph about how demo-only agents fail on network errors and pause/resume — an on-topic elaboration of the same failure-mode point, not a displacement of any expected idea.

A Theory for Choosing: Decision Axes Instead of Brands:
**1:** All four decision axes are present with matching substance: control-flow explicitness vs. autonomy, reliability primitives (with both required golden citations for LangGraph persistence and PydanticAI durable execution), abstraction/DX, and tooling interoperability (with the required FastMCP golden citation). The capstone mapping and the required Section 4 transition text are both present, closely paraphrasing the expected wording.

The Landscape Today: Frameworks, Philosophies & Adoption Snapshot:
**1:** All eight frameworks' philosophy-and-adoption content is present (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, AgentKit, CrewAI, PydanticAI, AutoGen, Claude Agent SDK, FastMCP), all seven images (4-10) are present, both required aside callouts (LangGraph vs. LangChain; AgentKit vs. Agents SDK) are present and near-verbatim, and the adoption-metrics/hybrid-pattern closing content is present. Content completeness is not in question here — the section's problem is length, not missing ideas (see guideline_adherence).

Framework Deep Dive: LangGraph:
**1:** Both sections cover the graph-based modeling approach, the three core production primitives (interrupts, persistence/checkpointing, time-travel debugging), the graph-API-vs-functional-API contrast, and the overkill-for-simple-scripts framing. All ideas are present with matching substance.

Framework Deep Dive: OpenAI Agents SDK:
**1:** Both sections cover the minimal-primitives philosophy, all five core concepts (Agents, Tools, Guardrails, Handoffs, Sessions), the execution-model contrast with LangGraph (paraphrased rather than verbatim, but the same substance and order), the fast-production-path strength, and the reliability trade-off.

Framework Deep Dive: AgentKit:
**1:** Both sections cover the lifecycle-toolkit positioning, all four named components (Agent Builder, Connector Registry, ChatKit, Evals/RFT), the "AgentKit sits one layer above the SDK" note, the ecosystem trade-off, and the value proposition. The Connector Registry description omits the guideline's specific named connectors (Dropbox, Drive, SharePoint, Teams) and the Evals/RFT bullet drops the specific examples (datasets, prompt optimization, custom graders) in favor of a compressed closing clause — both are single-item-style compressions of an illustrative list rather than missing ideas.

Framework Deep Dive: CrewAI:
**1:** Both sections cover the Crews/Flows dual architecture with matching definitions, the prototype-then-structure progression pattern (plus an added illustrative example, on-topic), the DX focus (CLI, YAML, memory/persistence), the researcher-to-writer sweet spot, and the opinionated-construct trade-off.

Framework Deep Dive: PydanticAI:
**1:** Both sections cover the FastAPI-like philosophy, the production features (durable execution via Temporal/DBOS/Prefect, plus Restate — traceable to the golden Durable Execution source — and built-in graph support), the ergonomics wins, the schema-investment trade-off, and the best-fit scenario tied to the writing agent's auditability needs.

Framework Deep Dive: AutoGen:
**1:** Both sections cover the layered design (Studio/AgentChat/Core as a three-item bulleted breakdown, matching the expected format), the explore-in-Studio-then-harden workflow, the explicit not-for-production disclaimer, the R&D-lab strength, and the re-implementation trade-off.

Framework Deep Dive: Claude Agent SDK:
**1:** Both sections cover the tight-integration philosophy, ergonomic tool calling tailored to Anthropic models, the three named trade-offs (smaller community, fewer integrations, evolving API), the opportunity-vs-risk framing, and the clearest-use-case statement.

Framework Deep Dive: FastMCP:
**1:** Both sections cover FastMCP's non-runtime role, the write-once-reuse-everywhere interoperability benefit, production extensions (auth, composition, cloud deployment), the capstone usage pattern, the tools-as-workflows aside (near-verbatim), and the Pythonic-decorator code example matching the golden Quickstart source exactly. The interoperability sentence drops the guideline's explicit "Claude Code" mention in favor of "any other compatible system" — a single dropped item inside an otherwise-covered list, consistent with not penalizing a single dropped list item.

Choosing for Your Project: Decision Matrix & Tentative Forecasts:
**1:** Table 1 matches the expected table cell-for-cell, including the verbatim title. The evolving-nature caveat, the per-framework forecasts (all six), and the three hybrid-pattern examples are all present, plus an added on-topic elaboration about enterprise use cases.

Our Capstone Pivots:
**1:** Both sections cover the initial LangGraph-for-both plan, the research agent's need for interactivity that broke the rigid-graph approach, the writing agent's opposite requirements, the resulting hybrid outcome (Nova as FastMCP server, Brown as LangGraph workflow with coarse MCP entry points), the emergent wrap-workflows-as-MCP-commands pattern, Brown's three named tools, and the OpenAI Agents SDK deprioritization reasoning.

Conclusion:
**1:** The core takeaway (stateful graphs, typed contracts, durable execution, MCP standardization), the MCP-spec-as-high-leverage-reading point, the practical selection process, and the AutoGen-Studio-to-FastMCP-to-LangGraph/PydanticAI migration path are all present. The forward-reference to the Nova build covers three of the guideline's five named parenthetical components (server/client, ingestion, Perplexity loops) and drops two ("filtering" and `research.md`); per standing guidance this partial coverage of the Nova forward-reference list is not treated as a substantive omission, so this does not cost CoreContent.
